explanation: Bronze is mostly copper with tin, and gave the Bronze Age its name. Steel is iron with a little carbon, usually under 2%, which makes it far stronger.

claims.text: An alloy is a material made by mixing a metal with other elements; bronze and steel are alloys.
An ore is a rock from which a metal is extracted, a compound is a substance of chemically bonded elements, and an oxide is a compound with oxygen; bronze and steel are none of these.
Bronze is an alloy made mostly of copper with tin.
The Bronze Age is named after bronze, the alloy its people used for tools and weapons.
Steel is iron with a small amount of carbon, usually less than 2%, which makes it much stronger than pure iron.
